title: Cohort of Patients With Systemic Granulomatosis and Associated Biological Collection
off: Cohort of Patients With Systemic Granulomatosis (Sarcoidosis and Other Systemic Granulomatoses) and Associated Biological Collection GRAMI-BIO Study

frSites.f: CHU de Bordeaux - service de Médecine Interne et Immunologie Clinique

summary: The GRAMI-BIO study is a prospective single-centre cohort study to recruit 150 patients followed up in the the Bordeaux University Hospital. The total duration of the GRAMI-BIO study is ten years (five years of inclusion with five years of follow-up): Consecutive inclusion of patients meeting the definition of systemic granulomatosis. The main objective of this cohort is to describe to clinical progression of systemic granulomatosis and to collect blood fraction samples (serum bank, plasma bank, urine bank, DNA bank) from subjects participating in the cohort.
desc: Systemic granulomatosis is a group of diseases whose common feature is the anatomopathological existence of giganto-cellular granulomas composed of macrophages, epithelial cells and CD4+ T lymphocytes. The exact cause of the development of these granulomas remains unknown, although numerous studies suggest the hypothesis of environmental factors (infectious, exposure to particles) and genetic susceptibility factors. The persistence of granulomas is deleterious, ultimately leading to local destruction and tissue damage resulting in fibrosis of neighbouring tissues. Granulomatosis is a heterogeneous group in terms of aetiology: schematically, either an aetiology is identified: infection, environmental factors (berylliosis, pneumoconiosis), iatrogenesis (drugs), neoplasia, immune deficiency; or granulomatosis is said to be idiopathic, the most common case, falling within the definition of systemic sarcoidosis. Therefore, with a view to future research work, it seems imperative to set up a biological bank of patients being monitored for systemic granulomatosis within the division. It is particularly important to identify genetic variants, circulating biomarkers associated with the onset, severity and response to treatment of these diseases. The main aim of the "GRAMI-BIO" study is to describe the clinical evolution of patients with systemic granulomatosis (sarcoidosis and other granulomatoses) followed at the Bordeaux University Hospital, and to collect samples from blood fractionation (serum bank, plasma bank, urine bank, DNA, RNA bank) to constitute a biobank.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients aged 18 or over
* Patients with systemic granulomatosis (diagnosis proven by anatomopathological sampling) at diagnosis.
* Persons affiliated to or benefiting from a social security scheme.
* Free, informed and written consent signed by the participant and the investigator (at the latest on the day of inclusion and before any examination required by the research).

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and/or Hepatitis C virus (HCV)
* Pregnant or breast-feeding women
* Patients already receiving specific treatment for systemic granulomatosis
* Persons deprived of their liberty by a judicial or administrative decision, minors, persons of legal age who are the object of a legal protection measure or unable to express their consent.

primary.m: Describe the clinical progression of systemic granulomatosis
primary.tf: At baseline (Day 0) and 60 months after baseline

x.titre: Cohorte de granulomatoses systémiques (sarcoïdose) avec biobanque, Bordeaux
x.question: Quelle est l'évolution clinique des patients atteints de granulomatose systémique, dont la sarcoïdose, suivis au CHU de Bordeaux ?
x.contexte:
Les granulomatoses systémiques réunissent des maladies dont le point commun est la présence de granulomes gigantocellulaires, formés de macrophages, de cellules épithélioïdes et de lymphocytes T CD4+. Leur cause exacte reste inconnue : des facteurs environnementaux (infections, exposition à des particules) et une susceptibilité génétique sont suspectés. La persistance des granulomes est délétère et conduit à une destruction locale puis à une fibrose des tissus voisins.

Ce groupe est hétérogène. Une étiologie peut être retrouvée (infection, bérylliose ou pneumoconiose, médicaments, néoplasie, déficit immunitaire), mais la forme idiopathique, correspondant à la sarcoïdose systémique, est la plus fréquente. Pour de futurs travaux, les investigateurs jugent indispensable de constituer une biobanque de patients suivis pour granulomatose systémique, afin d'identifier des variants génétiques et des biomarqueurs circulants associés à la survenue, à la sévérité et à la réponse au traitement. GRAMI-BIO est une cohorte prospective monocentrique de 150 patients inclus au diagnostic au CHU de Bordeaux (médecine interne et immunologie clinique), avec cinq ans d'inclusion et cinq ans de suivi. Elle prévoit des collections de sérum, plasma, urines, ADN et ARN.
x.interet: La cohorte décrira l'histoire naturelle de la sarcoïdose et des autres granulomatoses dans un centre expert. La biobanque servira de base à des recherches sur les biomarqueurs de sévérité et de réponse au traitement.
